checks: Brunn–Minkowski applies in each moving affine m-plane to the compact intersections with the prelimit body. The common body-volume normalization cancels on each row.

For fixed compact inputs, their open epsilon neighborhoods have Minkowski average inside the closed epsilon neighborhood of the sum. Lower Portmanteau for the inputs and upper Portmanteau for the containing output pass the inequality to the limit. Convexity of the support follows from positive masses in neighborhoods of support points.

The cited Borell theorem in Fradelizi–Guédon §2 uses compact tests of positive masses and the actual affine support dimension. Substitution of s=1/m gives q≤m, density exponent 1/(m−q) for q<m, and the constant-density endpoint for q=m. The positive-density root on the relative interior is continuous and the midpoint-ball tests give compact support and a bounded root.

The closed hypograph supplies a concave upper-semicontinuous representative and only changes boundary values. The centered-ball volume is exactly f by Fubini. Rescaling only hidden coordinates contracts support to the given plane while preserving the normalized projected law. The Dirac and uniform endpoints and the extra-height volume-one prism have the stated masses.

The simplex example has affine density root, and any higher power has positive second derivative along an interior line with varying coordinate sum. The cold-read result agrees with b9e8ea5c75ef1e0e §§1–2.

overlap.comparison: The accepted theorem assumes bounded Hausdorff-convergent fibers, vanishing total volume and a common normalization. It covers a thin subclass and a global lift. The new single-law theorem assumes only weak convergence in the ambient space and supplies the q=m endpoint, converse and sharpness.
The accepted graph lift starts from joint compactly supported concavity at every incidence. It uses ball sections but does not classify arbitrary weak limits or provide the sharp exponent example.

readability: The distinction between measure parameter 1/m and density power 1/(m−q) is explicit. The volume-one prism at the full-dimensional endpoint raises the intrinsic dimension by one.
review_method: Independent cold review of the frozen candidate, with exact arithmetic where applicable and comparison to its original source and pinned dependencies.
summary: Weak convergence in the ambient space, even with moving affine hulls, gives exactly the claimed three intrinsic law classes and the sharp thin realization.
